messages:
monitoring-bot: INCIDENT PAGE - streaming_p99 SLO breach detected for canary rollout r-2026-03-15-08. Metric: streaming_p99=2.8s (>2s SLO). Affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat-stream
alex: seeing the alert, i'm on it. pulling logs now.
priya: i'm joining. which canary id?
deploy-bot: Rollout r-2026-03-15-08 started by rafael at 08:12Z, target model encoder v7-quant. Canary 10% traffic. Status: IN_PROGRESS
rafael: yes that was the small encoder change + kv-layout tweak. i can revert if needed.
alex: tail traces show streaming stalls with long waits on `kv.get` calls. stack traces pinned to encoder host pool g-infer-enc-2a.
megan: any customer impact? support reports 2 customer sessions with stuttering audio transcripts.
sam: product: flagging potential SLO breach in customer-facing docs. we may need to notify tier-1 customers.
priya: metrics snippet:
```
path: /v1/chat-stream
p95: 420ms
p99: 2800ms
error_rate: 0.2%
kv.get_mean_ms: 12ms -> 220ms on enc-2a
```
alex: looks like KV cache fragmentation on encoder nodes after model weights changed. repeated kv.lock contention on shards.
rafael: encoder v7 changes local cache keys layout, might invalidate shard affinity. i didn't expect fragmentation at 10% traffic.
ops-bot: auto-remediation suggestion: roll traffic to baseline model v6, or reduce canary to 2%.
alex: immediate mitigation: reduce canary to 0% and pin 100% to v6 for stable routes. i'll run the command.
alex: running:
```
redwoodctl rollout set r-2026-03-15-08 --weight v7=0 --weight v6=100 --routes /v1/chat-stream,/v1/generate-stream
```
deploy-bot: Command executed: success. Canary weight updated: v7=0%, v6=100%
priya: good. watch p99s now.
rafael: i'll trigger a soft restart of encoder processes on g-infer-enc-2a to reclaim caches.
alex: ssh enc-2a-03 -> systemctl restart redwood-encoder
megan: i've patched a quick customer note in /support/incidents/321 with 'we're investigating increased tail latency; workaround applied'.
sam: please add an outbound note to affected enterprise customers if the p99 stays >2s after stabilization.
priya: p99 falling: 2.8s -> 1.1s over 3 minutes. looks like rollback helped.
ops-bot: incident severity: SEV2 -> de-escalating but keeping page open for postmortem.
rafael: root cause hypothesis: encoder v7 altered in-memory kv key hashing leading to hot shards and lock contention under multiplexed streaming workloads.
alex: collecting heap/kv histograms and wire traces for postmortem. saving traces to s3://redwood-incidents/4945671234/
megan: created customer update draft; PRRO: 'We've reverted the canary due to observed latency spikes affecting streaming. Engineers are investigating; no data loss. We'll follow up with RCA.'
sam: assign follow-up: ML eng to own RCA, Eng infra to propose kv migration strategy, product to coordinate customer comms.
priya: assigning owners: rafael (RCA), alex (infra traces + repl), sam (customer comms). i'll schedule postmortem at 16:00Z.
rafael: will prepare a diff to revert the kv-layout change and run a staging canary with unit tests for shard distribution.
alex: handoff: Tony (tony-oncall) is next on-call at 00:00Z. i'll leave notes in #oncall-handoff and include commands to re-weight traffic back if necessary.
ops-bot: handoff checklist created: https://redwood/internal/incidents/4945671234/checklist
tony-oncall: acknowledged. i'll monitor p99 until midnight and can re-open page if regression recurs.
monitoring-bot: ALERT CLEAR: streaming_p99 for /v1/chat-stream returned to 1.0s at 08:29Z. Incident status: Mitigated. Postmortem scheduled.
alex: thanks all — keeping thread open for RCA artifacts.
